raw.text:
As an archivist, my primary directive is the preservation of the tangible present before it is lost to irreversible disaster. While long-term pandemic-preparedness is a highly systematic and noble endeavor, an immediate flood poses an acute, time-sensitive threat to both human life and physical infrastructure—including the historical, cultural, and community records currently at risk of water damage and destruction. Once physical items and lives are lost to a flood, they cannot be recovered or re-archived. Therefore, I must prioritize the immediate stabilization and rescue efforts to preserve what currently exists. 

I am committing my choice now.
